chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Ubayda al-Hadhdha', from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

'Indeed, in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him) it is written that the false oath and the severing of family ties both cause houses to be deserted by their inhabitants, and block the womb — meaning the cutting-off of progeny.'

key_terms.الْيَمِينَ الْكَاذِبَةَ: False oath (yamin al-kadhiba) — an oath sworn falsely, one of the gravest sins in Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.بَلَاقِعَ: Desolate/deserted (balaqi') — a vivid classical Arabic term for places emptied of inhabitants
key_terms.تُنْغِلُ الرَّحِمَ: Blocks the womb (tunghill al-rahim) — a metaphor for preventing fertility and continuation of lineage
key_terms.قَطِيعَةَ الرَّحِمِ: Cutting of family ties (qati'at al-rahm) — severing relations with relatives, strongly condemned

ai.seo_question: What does the Book of Ali say about the consequences of false oaths and severing family ties?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) cites a ruling recorded in the Book of Ali (AS) — a revered text of jurisprudential and moral teachings compiled by Imam Ali — stating that false oaths and severing kinship ties bring two devastating worldly consequences: the abandonment of homes and the cessation of offspring. This teaching connects moral transgressions directly to social and biological destruction, warning early Muslim communities that such sins bring ruin not only to individuals but to their families and lineages.
